question: where do the 13 net questions (harness 0.8647 vs product 0.7669, multi-session, same answerer) die?
design: all 17 harness-only-correct questions re-run through the product retrieval stack locally (write_text seeding, orchestrated top-24, paragraph-primary, raw-first context under the runner's 20k budget); loss attributed to the first failing stage against the dataset's gold answer_session_ids: write (gold session has no paragraph), retrieval (stored but nothing surfaces in top-24), context (surfaced but assembled context lacks the gold answer text), answerer (context has the answer text). Counting intent via the harness runner's own counting_intent() heuristic.
findings: The write path loses NOTHING (0/17): paragraphs preserve every gold session verbatim - the earlier fidelity-audit worry is closed for this pool.

The dominant bucket is CONTEXT ASSEMBLY (11/17): gold sessions surface in top-24 but the raw-first, 20k-budget context lacks the answer text. 10 of the 11 are counting-intent questions - exactly what the harness's COUNT_FULL mechanism (prepend complete candidate sessions for counting questions) covers and the product has no equivalent of. This is a context-assembly feature gap, not a retrieval-component gap.

Retrieval losses (5/17) are ALL counting-intent too: counting questions need the complete enumeration of sessions, so top-24 recall of gold sessions is systematically harder for them - the harness's counting-intent branch also drives its retrieval composition.

Actionable direction (fits the review's no-new-retrieval-components constraint): productize the COUNT_FULL equivalent - counting/aggregation-intent queries get complete candidate sessions prepended to the answer context. Upper bound if all 15 counting-intent losses flip: 102+15=117/133 = 0.8796 on this pool (harness parity band).
honest_reading: 17 harness-only-correct minus 4 product-only-correct = the net 13; stage attribution is single-run retrieval (no SC variance here - retrieval is deterministic at temperature 0 embedding); the counting-intent heuristic is the harness's own keyword classifier, not a ground truth; the 0.8796 upper bound assumes every flipped loss scores correct (the harness scored these same questions correct with the same answerer, which bounds the assumption from above).
